Talk.Hello: Welcome! Take your time and look around.
Talk.Etched: The rune is set. See how it glows!
Talk.Creature: A fine beast. Take good care of it!
Talk.Formula: The {item} formula — copy it down carefully!

Shop.Featured: Featured — starred by the GM and listed first
Shop.OpenSheet: Open item sheet (or double-click the row)
Shop.PurseHint: How much the merchant can spend buying from you. It grows when you buy and refills a little each restock period.

Repair.Hint: Leave damaged or broken items here to have them restored to full HP. By the rules, destroyed items (0 HP) can't be repaired. To fix gear yourself, use Crafting's Repair action (10 minutes, repair toolkit).

Rune.Hint: Etch a rune from the shelf straight onto your gear (cost: the rune's Price). Property runes need a free slot (one per point of potency: +1, +2 …), and a greater version of a rune replaces the lesser one. By the rules, etching takes as long as crafting — the GM decides.
Rune.Unmodelled: PF2e doesn't track this rune on the sheet — buy it as an item and settle it with the GM
Rune.DoesNotFit: Can't be etched onto this item
Rune.NoSlot: No free property rune slot ({n} slots)
Rune.SameKind: Only between items of the same kind (weapon ↔ weapon, armor ↔ armor)
Rune.TransferHint: Move a rune from one item to another. Cost: 10% of the rune's Price (10% of both when swapping fundamental runes) plus the work fee. Free when moving from a runestone (GM Core).
Rune.UpgradeHint: Rules: upgrading to a stronger rune costs only the difference in Price (GM Core).

Trade.NoGM: A GM must be online to trade.
Trade.Timeout: No response. Check that a GM is online.

Err.NotYours: You don't have permission to trade as that character.
Err.NoPurse: The merchant can't afford it (funds {have}, needs {need}).

Restock.Nothing: {shop}: nothing came in this time (failed rolls, or already full)

Edit.Title: Edit shop — {name}
Edit.DropHint: Drop items from a compendium or the sidebar here to stock them. Drop a roll table to roll it and stock the results.
Edit.PerDayHint: How many come back each day. 0 = never, -1 = back to max after a day
Edit.FeaturedHint: Featured (★): shown first in the shop with a star
Edit.EmptyStock: Nothing on the shelf. Pick goods on the 'Add goods' tab, or drop them here.
Edit.TemplatesHint: Stocks goods suited to the party level for each kind of shop in one go, and turns on the matching services (repair, rune forge, items bought). Can be used more than once.
Edit.NoScrollTemplate: Couldn't find a base scroll/wand item for that rank.
Edit.ChanceHint: Chance of coming back in a single restock. Blank: the rarity default (Settings tab)
Edit.OneDayHint: Restock once (using the shop's rule: fixed amount or chance rolls)
Edit.AddFormula: Sell as a formula (click again to remove)
Edit.FoodHint: The Rutz food catalog (the same items as Rutz's PF2e Gacha and Days). Cheap food: a DC 5 flat check after eating, or fatigued; fine and luxury food: temporary HP. Uses the quantity / ∞ setting above.

Tpl.Name: Name
Tpl.StepsHint: A template is a list of steps. Each step finds catalog items matching its filters (category, level, rarity, magic) and stocks a random number of them. Levels are relative to the party level (−3 … +2); 'max' is an absolute cap. Blank = no limit.
Tpl.CountHint: How many to pick at random (0 = all that match)
Tpl.HitsHint: Items that match at party level {level}
Tpl.ResetAsk: Reset the template '{name}' to the module default?

Set.Title: Shop name
Set.RatesHint: Rules: items usually sell for half their Price (GM Core p. 48). Plentiful items may fetch only 25% or 10%, or be refused. Treasure such as gems and art objects sells at full price if that setting is on.
Set.Resell: Put what players sell on the shelf (they can buy it back later)
Set.AutoRestock: Restock automatically each time a game day passes
Set.RepairHint: The rules set no repair price; the GM decides. Percent: Price × rate × fraction of HP lost.
Set.RuneTransfer: Rune transfers (10% of the rune's Price)
Set.RuneHint: Etch runes from the shelf straight onto customers' gear.
Set.ChanceHint: Each period, every line secretly rolls d100; if it's within the chance, its restock amount comes in. Lines can have their own chance on the Shelf tab.
Set.MaterialHint: Multiplier on the reforging cost (the difference in value).
Set.WealthApplyHint: Sets the selling/buying rates and shop funds to this wealth level's suggested values (party level from the Add goods tab).
Set.PurseHint: Buying from players is paid from these funds. When they run out the shop stops buying — so endless crafting and selling can't print money. Funds grow again when players buy.
Set.MaterialReach: Show materials up to character level +
Set.FormulaShelf: Also sell the formulas of what's on the shelf
Set.FormulaHint: Price = Player Core formula price (level 0: 5 sp, 1: 1 gp, 5: 8 gp, 10: 50 gp …) × multiplier. Uncommon and rarer formulas have no price in the rules, so the GM's multiplier applies. Use 📜 on the Add goods tab to add formulas for items not on the shelf.
Set.FeeHint: Charged on top of the rules price (the new rune's Price / the difference / 10%) for etching, upgrading and transferring runes, and for changing materials.

Ev.Hint: An active event overrides the shop's base rates (sells {buy}% · buys {sell}%) — enter values as a % of the list price. Leave a field blank to keep that rate. With categories checked it applies only to those, and category events take priority over shop-wide ones (among equals, the lower event wins). E.g. buys at 100% = pays the full list price.
Ev.Name: Event name
Ev.BuyHint: What players pay, as a % of the list price (blank: the shop's own rate)
Ev.SellHint: What the shop pays players, as a % of the list price (blank: the shop's own rate)

Manager.Title: Shops
Manager.ChatHint: Post a shop invitation to chat
Manager.DayHint: Restock every shop by one day (game time doesn't change)
Manager.TimeHint: Advance game time by one day (shops that follow game time restock on their own)
Manager.None: No shops yet. Create one with 'New shop'.
Manager.NoneOpen: No shop is open right now.
Manager.Name: Name
Manager.NewHint: Shops are created as loot actors. To move one to another world, use Export (JSON) or put the actor in a compendium.

Dur.Title: Durability
Dur.Hint: Damage to an item is reduced by its Hardness before it loses HP. At or below the Broken Threshold (BT) it's broken; at 0 HP it's destroyed and can't be repaired. Broken armor automatically gets its AC status penalty as an effect (light −1, medium −2, heavy −3). In PF2e only shields have HP, so use 'Material…' to give weapons and armor GM Core material values.
Dur.NoHp: No HP — pick a material to give it durability
Dur.MaterialHint: Hardness/HP/BT from the GM Core material table
Dur.BrokenArmorDesc: Broken armor keeps its item bonus but takes a status penalty to AC (light −1, medium −2, heavy −3). Player Core p. 269.
Dur.GuessHint: Apply durability from the suggested material (GM Core: metal weapons and armor are iron or steel)

NoticeState.broken: A broken item doesn't function normally (armor: AC penalty; shield: no Shield Block). It needs repair.

Settings.LogHint: Who sees buy and sell messages in chat.
Settings.LogInvolved: The trading player and the GM
Settings.TreasureHint: Gems, art objects and other treasure are bought at full Price regardless of the shop's buying rate.
Settings.BrokenArmorHint: When worn armor breaks, add its AC status penalty as an effect; remove it once repaired.
Settings.PacksHint: Comma-separated pack IDs. Blank: the equipment packs enabled in the compendium browser (translation packs first).
Settings.RenameRunes: Rename items when runes are etched
Settings.RenameRunesHint: Etching or transferring runes at a rune forge adds the runes to the item's name (e.g. +1 Striking Flaming Longsword). The original name is remembered.
Settings.DurMarks: Mark damaged gear on character sheets
Settings.DurMarksHint: Adds a small mark next to the name of items that have lost Hit Points (damaged, broken, destroyed). Undamaged gear gets no mark.
Settings.DurNoticeHint: When an item loses Hit Points, the character's players and the GM get a whisper (highlighted when it breaks).
Settings.Minion: Bought animals get the minion trait
Settings.MinionHint: Animals (NPCs) bought at a shop get the minion trait — they act only when commanded.
Settings.InvLogHint: When a player character gains or loses items or coins outside the Rutz modules (dragged from a compendium or the Items tab, taken from a merchant or loot, the sheet's sell button, direct edits), post it to chat with its source. Using items up (drinking potions, firing arrows) isn't logged.
Settings.InvLogGMHint: Off (default): changes the GM makes directly to a player character's inventory aren't logged.

Creature.Hint: Buying creates an NPC actor owned by the character's player (Actors tab, 'Bought Animals' folder). This is an animal bought with coin, separate from the Animal Companion class feature.
Creature.EditHint: Creatures (NPCs) this shop sells. Find and add them from your Actor compendiums (bestiaries) below. Prices follow the Player Core animals table (riding horse 8 gp, warhorse 30 gp, guard dog 2 sp …); animals not on the table are priced by level. You can change prices any time.
Creature.Loading: Reading bestiaries… (only slow the first time)

Material.LevelHint: The material's item level — after reforging, the item's level and rarity follow this material
Material.Hint: Follows the GM Core precious materials table. Cost = (value of the same item in the new material − its current value, runes included, as priced by PF2e) × the smithy rate. Hardness and HP change to the new material's, and the material is added to the end of the name (custom names are kept). The rules have no activity for changing an existing item's material, so this 'reforging' is a house rule.

MatInfo.adamantine: Extremely hard; overcomes resistances that only adamantine bypasses.
MatInfo.cold-iron: Extra damage to creatures with a weakness to cold iron (demons, fey …).
MatInfo.silver: Extra damage to creatures with a weakness to silver (devils, werecreatures …).
MatInfo.dawnsilver: Light: less Bulk, and armor is easier to wear.
MatInfo.duskwood: Light wood: less Bulk, and armor is easier to wear.
MatInfo.dragonhide: Dragonhide: protection against that dragon's damage type.
MatInfo.orichalcum: The metal of time: a weapon can hold one more property rune.

Hint.poor: Few goods (common only), a little pricey (110%). Pays 40%, and its small funds run out fast.
Hint.modest: An ordinary shop. Common goods, sells at 100%, pays 50%.
Hint.rich: 1.5× the goods, uncommon items too. Pays 50%, ample funds.
Hint.lavish: 2.5× the goods, uncommon and rare items, level range +2. Luxury prices (105%). Large funds: buys treasure and expensive items too.

Cuisine.aleDesc: A mug of ale (Player Core, Basic Services).
Cuisine.teaDesc: A pot of coffee or tea.
Cuisine.poorMealDesc: Bread and thin gruel. Counts as a day's food (Rutz's PF2e Days).
Cuisine.squareMealDesc: A hot, filling meal. Counts as a day's food (Rutz's PF2e Days).
Cuisine.fineDiningDesc: A course from a renowned cook. Counts as a day's food (Rutz's PF2e Days).

Formula.Hint: A bought formula goes into the character's formula book (copying it in takes 1 hour, per Player Core). Prices follow the formula price table by item level.

Inv.Title: Inventory log
Inv.FromSheet: Source: edited on the sheet (new item, or quantity/coins changed)
